name: Color swatch
description: Round colour options for picking one colour, as for a tag, a list or a drawing tool. It can include a "no colour" option and an "any colour" option that opens the colour picker.

classes.ayy-swatch: One colour: a <label> around a native radio (which stays in the page but draws nothing), or a <button aria-pressed>. Set --ayy-swatch on it to the colour, a token: var(--ayy-chart-1…6), var(--ayy-accent-*), var(--ayy-color-destructive). The radio (or the button) needs an aria-label naming the colour.
classes.ayy-swatch--none: "No colour": the surface with a red diagonal stroke. No --ayy-swatch.
classes.ayy-swatch--custom: Any colour: a <label> around an <input type="color">, drawn as a ring of the chart colours around the picked colour. Clicking it opens ayywi's built-in ColorPicker in a floating popover instead of the OS picker (React and @danitesler/ayywi/elements keep --ayy-swatch in step with the input).
classes.ayy-swatch-popover: Popover container for ayywi's ColorPicker opened by a custom swatch: top layer (popover="auto"), positioned next to the swatch dot.
classes.ayy-swatch-group: Wrapping row of swatches: role="radiogroup" with an aria-label or aria-labelledby. Padded so the picked ring and focus ring aren't clipped.
classes.ayy-swatch-group--track: On a pill-shaped wash, like a toolbar's colour row.

default.looks: A round dot in --ayy-swatch with a hairline so light and dark colours both show. none is the surface crossed by a red stroke; custom is a rainbow ring around the current colour.

pressed.none: No pressed look; it's picked as soon as it's clicked (see selected).

focus.when: :focus-visible on the button, or on the radio inside
focus.looks: 2px ring, 5px offset, outside the picked ring.

selected.looks: A gap in the surface colour, a ring in the text colour, and a tick on the dot, not colour alone. Forced colours: Highlight outline.

error.none: A colour can't be invalid. Pick a default instead of leaving none picked.

loading.none: Colours are local; no loading look.

scale.sm: 0.6 × the sm control height: about 17px compact, 19 comfortable, 24 touch.
scale.md: 0.75 × the sm control height: 21px compact, 24 comfortable, 30 touch.
scale.lg: The sm control height: 28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch.

sizes.density: Dot size follows data-density (above); the hit area always reaches the sm control height.
sizes.width: Square. A group wraps onto more lines; track (ayy-swatch-group--track) puts them on a pill.

js: colorSwatchClass({ size?, none?, custom?, className? }), colorSwatchGroupClass({ track?, className? }) → string; syncColorSwatch(input) shows a custom swatch's colour; usesColorPicker(input) checks Popover API support; openSwatchColorPicker(input) opens ayywi's ColorPicker in a popover; openColorPickerFrom(event) intercepts mousedown/click/keydown on custom swatches.

react.import: import { ColorSwatch, ColorSwatchButton, ColorSwatchCustom, ColorSwatchGroup } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

props.color: string — a CSS colour, ideally a token ("var(--ayy-chart-2)")
props.label: string — the colour's name, required ("Blue")
props.name: string — the same for every swatch in the group

props.label: string — required ("Custom colour")
Every <input type="color"> prop: value, defaultValue (hex), onChange.

a11y: Radio swatches are native: Tab enters the group, arrow keys move the pick, and screen readers say the colour's name and "checked". Every swatch needs a name (label prop / aria-label) because a dot has no text.
Name the group ("Tag colour") with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
The picked swatch has a ring and a tick, not just a colour; light and dark dots keep a hairline edge in every theme. High Contrast outlines the picked one with the system highlight.
The dot is smaller than a touch target, but its hit area reaches a control's height (bigger at touch density).
do: Use swatches to pick a colour from a short, fixed set: a tag, a list, a calendar, an annotation pen.
Colour them with tokens (--ayy-chart-1…6 are made to be told apart and meet 3:1 on every surface), and name each one.
Offer a none swatch when "no colour" is a real choice, and a ColorSwatchCustom when people may need any colour (an image editor).
Use a track group in a toolbar, size sm.
dont: Don't use swatches to choose a theme or a status — use a Segmented control or a Select; colour alone doesn't say what a status means.
Don't hardcode hex values in --ayy-swatch; use tokens, or the app's own colour variables when people pick colours (stored values belong in data, not in markup).
Don't show more than about ten swatches in a row — group them, or add a ColorSwatchCustom.
Don't use colour names that only make sense in one theme ("Black" turns white in dark mode) — name the role ("Ink").
